title: Worker container entrypoint: clone, implement, push branch and RESULT, exit
description:
The container-side half of 0ds. 0ds landed the dispatch layer — probe, confirmed dispatch, expiring liveness, concurrent fan-out, git-only collect — and it is tested, but nothing exists for it to boot. A worker container needs its own entrypoint, distinct from the orchestrator entrypoint in cloud/sandbox/entrypoint.sh: clone at the epic base, branch tick/<epic>/<tick>, run the harness on one tick, push the branch plus RESULT-<tick>.md, exit with a code that distinguishes the failure classes the way the orchestrator entrypoint already does.

Constraints already measured, do not re-derive: on Cloudflare an image belongs to the containers application rather than to a boot (x3v), so a worker runs the same image as the orchestrator and must be told which role it is playing. Fan-out per-sandbox time degrades 3.74x at N=5 and kuf found ALL of that in dependency install, not the image pull — so whatever this entrypoint does about dependencies is the performance question for the whole per-tick design. max_instances = 3 will silently serialise a wider wave.

The probe 0ds runs must have something real to check for: define the marker here, in the entrypoint, rather than leaving dispatch to guess.
